title: Tanzanian Goat Coconut Curry
community: Swahili coast — the richest celebration goat preparation
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Mchuzi wa Mbuzi wa Nazi — Tanzanian goat coconut curry. Young goat slow-cooked until falling-tender in a deeply spiced coconut milk and tomato sauce. The most luxurious goat preparation on the Tanzanian coast — served at weddings and major celebrations.
longDesc: Goat coconut curry is the Swahili coast's most celebratory goat dish — the combination of slowly cooked young goat and rich coconut milk produces a sauce of extraordinary depth. It is served at weddings and major celebrations where only the best food will do.
steps: Cook onions until very golden — 10 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger, all spices. Stir 1 minute.
Add tomatoes. Cook 10 minutes until very thick.
Return goat. Add water. Simmer covered 70—80 minutes until very tender.
Add coconut milk. Simmer gently 12 minutes.
chefTips: Young goat (mbuzi mdogo) is non-negotiable for this dish.
The tomato base must be very thick before adding water.
Coconut milk goes in only after the goat is fully tender.
commonMistakes: Old goat — too tough even after long cooking.
cookingScience: Young goat contains less mature collagen than older animals — it converts to gelatin faster and more completely, producing the characteristically silky, rich sauce.
sustainabilityTips: Young Tanzanian goat from pastoral communities.
healthBenefits: Goat is leaner than beef or lamb.
culturalNote: Goat coconut curry is the coastal Tanzanian dish that signals the highest level of hospitality — when a host serves this, they are saying: you matter, this occasion matters, and nothing has been spared in preparing for you.
